newsitem.title: USA: Kennedy library releases secret tape recordings.
newsitem.headline: Kennedy library releases secret tape recordings.

text.p: The library of President John F. Kennedy released on Thursday 24 hours of secret tape recordings made in the White House in 1963, including conversations about U.S. policy in Vietnam.

The recordings, made from August through October, 1963, include discussions of events leading up to the assassination of South Vietnam's President Ngo Dinh Diem in November, 1963, just weeks before Kennedy was killed.

"I don't think you're going to find any bombshells in this," said Stephanie Fawcett, senior foreign policy archivist with the John Fitzgerald Kennedy Library in Boston. "You get to see the president in a decision-making process. You hear it come from his mouth what that position is," she said.
The library is making the tapes available to the public.

Historians may find it interesting to hear Kennedy's Secretary of Defence, Robert McNamara, considered a hawk during the Vietnam War, advocating the withdrawal of advisors in the early stages of U.S. involvement in the Southeast Asian conflict, Fawcett said.
President Kennedy is heard searching for other options in Vietnam, though he expressly said he wanted to win the war there, she said.
"I think the president was trying to walk a very cautious line, neither for withdrawal or escalation," she said.
The tape recorders were likely installed for Kennedy's memoirs and were activated by hidden switches at his desk in the Oval Office and at his seat in the Cabinet Room, she said.

The crude recordings are sometimes indecipherable, catching squeaking chairs, pipes being banged on ashtrays, and other outside noises. They were probably done with only the president's knowledge, Fawcett said.

About 185 hours of Kennedy White House recordings from July, 1962 to just weeks before he was assassinated in November 1963 were expected to be declassified over the next five years under a 1995 federal law requiring swift release of all sensitive materials, she said.
Last October, the library released more than 15 hours of tapes made in October, 1962 at the time of the Cuban Missile Crisis.
